newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks rally at start, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks rally at start, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: A powerful rally in the bond market, sparked by favorable economic data, carried Wall Street stocks higher in early trading Tuesday.
The Dow industrials surged 78 points, or 1.15 percent, to 6861, triggering the NYSE's automatic curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 0934 EDT/1334 GMT.
The long bond was up 1-9/32 to yield 7.01 percent.
Bonds rallied after the release of a weaker than forecast first quarter Employment Cost Index, an indicator known to be closely watched by the Federal Reserve.
"This is a massive short squeeze. The bulls have the bears by the tail, at least over the near term," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

"With the (long bond) yield at seven percent again, if you have been betting against the market in the near term you have to stop your loss here. You have to be long or be wrong. That's the story here."
He said strength was broad, trickling down to small-caps.
Financial sector stocks were among the beneficiaries of the falling yield, with Citicorp up 3-7/8 at 111-1/8, Chase Manhattan Corp up 2-3/4 at 90-1/4 and J.P. Morgan & Co up 1-5/8 at 99-3/4.
High techs put in a strong showing, with Intel Corp, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, up 2-5/8 at 148-7/8, Cisco Systems Inc up 1-3/8 at 47-7/8 and Microsoft Corp up 1-7/8 at 116-3/4.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 17 points, or 1.37 percent, at 1234.
